questions.question: What does EC2 stand for?

explanation.correct: EC2 stands for Elastic Compute Cloud — AWS's virtual server service.
explanation.why: Container = ECS, Cluster ≠ EC2, Core is not an AWS term.

questions.question: Which AWS service model does EC2 fall under?

explanation.correct: EC2 is Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) — the user manages OS and software; AWS manages hardware.
explanation.why: PaaS = Elastic Beanstalk, SaaS = end-user applications, FaaS = Lambda.

questions.question: What is an AMI in AWS?

options.text: A hardware configuration for EC2 instances
A software configuration template containing OS and applications

explanation.correct: AMI (Amazon Machine Image) is a software configuration template — it contains the OS, libraries, utilities, and optionally applications.
explanation.why: Hardware configuration = instance type. Security rules = security group. Scaling = Auto Scaling.

questions.question: What is the default username for an Amazon Linux EC2 instance?

explanation.correct: The default user for Amazon Linux is ec2-user. You log in as ec2-user, not root.
explanation.why: ubuntu is the default user for Ubuntu instances. root is not used for direct SSH login by default.

questions.question: Which port does SSH use by default?

explanation.correct: SSH uses port 22. You must open port 22 in your Security Group to allow SSH connections.
explanation.why: Port 80 = HTTP, Port 443 = HTTPS, Port 3389 = RDP (Windows remote desktop).

questions.question: Where is the public key stored in key pair authentication?

explanation.correct: The public key is automatically stored on the EC2 instance when you create a key pair. The private key is kept on your laptop.
explanation.why: Never the other way around — your private key stays local, the public key goes to the server.

questions.question: What is EBS in the context of EC2?

options.text: A networking component for routing traffic
A virtual hard drive (block storage) attached to EC2
An event bus for serverless applications

explanation.correct: EBS (Elastic Block Storage) is the virtual hard disk for your EC2 instance. Default size is 8 GB.
explanation.why: Event bus = EventBridge. S3 encryption is a different service. EBS is specifically block storage for EC2.

questions.question: What does a Security Group do for an EC2 instance?

options.text: Controls inbound and outbound network traffic (virtual firewall)

explanation.correct: A Security Group is a virtual firewall — it defines rules for what network traffic is allowed in (inbound) and out (outbound) of your EC2 instance.
explanation.why: EBS encryption is separate. IAM handles user permissions. CloudWatch handles monitoring.

questions.question: What are the two formats in which an EC2 private key file can be downloaded?

explanation.correct: .pem is used with OpenSSH (Linux/macOS/modern Windows). .ppk is used with PuTTY on Windows.
explanation.why: JSON/YAML are config formats. .key and .cert are TLS certificate formats, not key pair formats.

questions.question: Which EC2 instance type is free tier eligible?

explanation.correct: t2.micro (1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM) is free tier eligible — 750 hours/month for the first 12 months.
explanation.why: t2.large, m5.xlarge, and c5.2xlarge are all paid instances. Only micro-sized general purpose instances qualify for free tier.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the instance type in EC2 configuration?

options.text: It defines the operating system to be installed
It controls firewall rules for the instance
It determines the hardware configuration (vCPU, RAM, storage)
It specifies the geographic location of the server

explanation.correct: Instance type defines hardware — vCPU count, RAM, and associated storage options. AMI defines software; Security Group defines firewall; Region defines location.
explanation.why: A common exam trap — AMI vs instance type. One is software, one is hardware.

questions.question: By default, EC2 does not allow which type of authentication for SSH?

explanation.correct: By default, EC2 disables password-based SSH authentication for security. Key pair authentication is used instead.
explanation.why: Passwords can be guessed or stolen. Key pairs use cryptographic files that are much harder to compromise.

questions.question: You launch an EC2 instance without selecting an Availability Zone. What happens?

options.text: AWS automatically selects an Availability Zone within your chosen region
The instance is launched in us-east-1a by default
You are prompted to select one before proceeding

explanation.correct: If you don't specify an Availability Zone, AWS automatically selects one within your chosen region. The region selection is always required; AZ selection is optional.
explanation.why: AWS never fails a launch just because AZ wasn't specified — it handles this automatically.

questions.question: Which EC2 instance type family would you choose for a high-traffic relational database requiring lots of caching?

explanation.correct: Memory Optimized instances (r-family) are designed for high RAM workloads like databases and in-memory caching. They provide a higher ratio of RAM to vCPU.
explanation.why: General purpose = balanced; Compute Optimized = high CPU; Storage Optimized = high disk I/O.

questions.question: What happens to your EC2 application files when you stop an instance to change its instance type?

options.text: All files are lost — you need to redeploy
Files are backed up to S3 automatically
Files are preserved on EBS — the storage is unaffected by instance type changes
Files are moved to a temporary storage until restart

explanation.correct: EBS volumes are attached independently of the instance type. Changing CPU/RAM (instance type) does not affect the EBS volume or its contents.
explanation.why: You're changing one layer (compute) while storage remains a separate, independent layer.

questions.question: Which service inside EC2 listens on port 22 and handles SSH login requests?

explanation.correct: SSHD (SSH Daemon) is a background service (daemon) on Linux that continuously listens on port 22 and handles incoming SSH connection requests.
explanation.why: HTTPD handles HTTP, FTPD handles FTP, SMBD handles Samba/file sharing.

questions.question: What is the key difference between inbound and outbound rules in a Security Group?

options.text: Inbound rules control traffic from EC2 to the internet; outbound is the reverse
Inbound rules control traffic entering the EC2 instance; outbound controls traffic leaving
Inbound rules apply to HTTP traffic only; outbound applies to SSH
There is no difference — Security Groups are symmetrical

explanation.correct: Inbound rules control what traffic is allowed TO reach your EC2 instance. Outbound rules control what traffic can leave your EC2 instance.
explanation.why: Common exam trap — inbound is incoming TO the instance, outbound is traffic FROM the instance.

questions.question: If you want to host a public website on EC2, which two Security Group inbound rules do you minimally need?

explanation.correct: You need SSH (port 22) to manage the server, and HTTP (port 80) to allow public web traffic. Add HTTPS (443) if you set up SSL.
explanation.why: FTP (21) is insecure and not used here. RDP (3389) is for Windows remote desktop, not web hosting.

questions.question: What is the correct SSH command format to connect to an Amazon Linux EC2 instance?

explanation.correct: The correct format is: ssh -i [key file] [username]@[IP]. For Amazon Linux, the username is ec2-user. The -i flag specifies the identity (private key) file.
explanation.why: ubuntu is for Ubuntu instances. root login is disabled by default. -p 22 isn't needed since 22 is default.

questions.question: You run the SSH command but get 'WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!' and connection is refused. What's likely wrong?

options.text: The EC2 instance is not running
The .pem file has incorrect permissions — it's too open
SSH is not installed on your laptop
The Security Group is blocking port 443

explanation.correct: On Linux/macOS, SSH requires the .pem file to have permissions 400 (owner read-only). If it's too open (e.g., 644), SSH rejects it. Fix with: chmod 400 mykey.pem
explanation.why: On Windows this warning may appear differently but the cause is the same — file permission security.

questions.question: Your EC2 instance's public IP changes every time you stop and start it. What AWS feature would you use to assign a permanent public IP?

explanation.correct: An Elastic IP is a static, fixed public IP address you can allocate and attach to an EC2 instance. It does not change when you stop/start the instance.
explanation.why: VPC Peering = network connectivity between VPCs. NAT Gateway = outbound internet for private instances. Route 53 = DNS.

questions.question: Which EC2 instance type family would you choose for a machine learning training job with GPU requirements?

explanation.correct: Accelerated Computing instances (p and g families) include GPU hardware designed for machine learning, AI training, graphics rendering, and other GPU-intensive workloads.
explanation.why: General purpose = balanced; Memory = high RAM; Storage = high disk. None have GPUs.

questions.question: What is the naming structure of EC2 instance types? What do the components of 't3.large' mean?

options.text: t = tier, 3 = vCPU count, large = RAM amount
t = instance family (general purpose), 3 = generation, large = size
t = type, 3 = pricing tier, large = storage size
t = test/production flag, 3 = AZ count, large = network bandwidth

explanation.correct: Instance type naming: [family][generation].[size]. t = general purpose family, 3 = third generation, large = size tier.
explanation.why: The letter represents the instance family. The number represents the generation (newer = better performance/cost). The suffix is the size.

questions.question: Security Groups are described as 'stateful'. What does this mean?

options.text: They maintain session data between requests
Return traffic for allowed inbound connections is automatically permitted without explicit outbound rules
Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins

explanation.correct: Stateful means if you allow an inbound SSH connection, the response traffic is automatically allowed outbound — you don't need a separate outbound rule.
explanation.why: This contrasts with Network ACLs (NACLs) which are stateless — you must explicitly allow both inbound and outbound.

questions.question: A company needs servers that can handle extremely high disk read/write operations for a Hadoop cluster. Which instance family should they use?

explanation.correct: Storage Optimized instances (i and d families) are designed for workloads requiring very high sequential read/write operations — like Hadoop, Cassandra, and data warehousing.
explanation.why: Hadoop is I/O bound — it reads and writes massive amounts of data. This needs storage optimization, not CPU or RAM optimization.

questions.question: You need to run the same web application on 10 identical EC2 instances for high availability. What is the most efficient approach to ensure they all have the same configuration?

options.text: Manually configure each instance one by one
Create a custom AMI from a configured instance and launch all 10 from that AMI
Use the same key pair and security group
Use copy-paste in the EC2 launch wizard

explanation.correct: You configure one instance exactly as needed, then create a custom AMI (snapshot of that configuration). All 10 instances launched from that AMI will be identical — OS, software, config all pre-installed.
explanation.why: This is a key use case for custom AMIs: replicable, identical environments at scale.

questions.question: An EC2 instance in a private subnet needs to update its packages from the internet. It has no public IP. What AWS component enables this?

explanation.correct: A NAT Gateway allows instances in private subnets to initiate outbound connections to the internet (e.g., for updates) without having a public IP or being directly accessible from the internet.
explanation.why: Internet Gateway is for public subnets. VPC Peering connects VPCs, not internet access. Security Groups control traffic, not routing.

questions.question: What is the difference between stopping and terminating an EC2 instance?

options.text: Stopping = temporary pause (EBS preserved); Terminating = permanent deletion (EBS deleted by default)
Stopping = permanent deletion; Terminating = temporary pause
Both stopping and terminating delete the EBS volume
Stopping deletes EBS; Terminating preserves it

explanation.correct: Stopping an instance pauses it — EBS is preserved, you can restart. Terminating permanently deletes the instance and its root EBS volume (by default). You stop paying for compute when stopped, but EBS storage charges continue.
explanation.why: This is a critical exam and practical distinction — never terminate if you just want to pause billing temporarily.

questions.question: You create a key pair in the AWS Mumbai region. Can you use the same key pair to SSH into an EC2 instance in the US-East-1 region?

options.text: Yes, key pairs are global and work across all regions
No, key pairs are region-specific and must be created in each region separately
Yes, but only if both instances use the same AMI
No, key pairs only work with instances in the same availability zone

explanation.correct: Key pairs are region-specific in AWS. A key pair created in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) cannot be used in us-east-1. You must create a separate key pair in each region you use.
explanation.why: This catches many beginners — if you switch regions and can't SSH, check whether you created a key pair in that region.

questions.question: A developer wants to allow SSH access to an EC2 instance only from their company's office IP (203.0.113.10). What is the correct Security Group inbound rule?

explanation.correct: To restrict SSH to a single IP: Protocol = SSH, Port = 22, Source = 203.0.113.10/32. The /32 CIDR notation means exactly that one IP address.
explanation.why: /0 = all IPs (0.0.0.0/0 = anywhere). /32 = exactly one IP. /24 = 256 IPs. Using /32 with a specific IP is the most restrictive and secure rule.
